Cp.bar_b_note: The HUD is compact, but its near-black boxes, outlined text and a dim, flat-lit orange interior fall well short of Palworld's clean, light interface and Valheim-class interior light.

Ut.bar_b_note: The fleece-and-horn ram reads close to the owner's Stormcapra bar, but on a neutral stage it shows no world light or atmosphere, and B's faint frames twist into an unreadable upturned, floating heap.

Oc.bar_b_note: The meadow has warm grass and blue distance, but the reward nodes are tiny, generic blobs and crates lost in a uniform grass carpet with flat midday light.

Vh.bar_b_note: B's per-site aftermaths (banners down, cage opened, crates smashed, smoke) carry the story, but smeared low-resolution terrain and flat light sink both sides against Palworld.

Nh.bar_b_note: A's braced timber frame with cap and stone footing starts to read as a built wall, but it is still one thin isolated panel, and B is a blown-out white card.

Ty.bar_b_note: The oak grove and path framing are pleasant, but the pickups are small, low-contrast blobs with no readable item identity and no grounding light.

Ky.bar_b_note: The glowing capture orb is a nice beat, but the tight top-down frames are filled with a blurry, cropped foreground companion and flat green grass, with no horizon.

Mq.bar_b_note: The grandpa reads warmly, with a clean silhouette and an earthy green-brown palette, but the large-eyed cartoon face leans further toward toy-like than the stylised realism of Palworld and the key art.

Qb.bar_b_note: A bright sky, a lake and a cottage set the scene, but the creatures are small mid-ground figures whose hurt and moving poses barely differ, and an oversized dark foreground grass mass takes up much of the frame.

Tp.bar_b_note: Brookfail, Pipwing and Bramblebun all stand at or below the trainer's height and read as small props, unlike Palworld's large, readable creature silhouettes.

Yq.bar_b_note: Creatures sit in grass tufts that soften their feet, and the dark, oversized foreground grass blocks dominate the lower half of the frame instead of framing the subject.

Ne.bar_b_note: Mira, Tam and Oskar now match their portraits in front of a charming timber-and-stone village, but the chibi characters and flat midday light stop short of Palworld and Valheim finish.

top_changes.change: Scale every Meadows creature clearly above the 1.80 m trainer and give it higher-contrast rim light, so creatures become the largest, most readable subjects in the Qb, Tp, Yq and Ky frames
Replace generic crates, orbs and glow plants with distinct, larger item-shaped pickup and harvest meshes (candy, potion, tonic, pack), each with its own silhouette and colour (Oc, Ty)

Fix the low-resolution, smeared terrain texture and the dark, oversized foreground grass blocks, and reframe the catch camera so the player, companion and target stay in one readable shot (Vh, Qb, Tp, Yq, Ky)
